questions.response: Use well-prepared soil, compost, and water regularly.
Plant teff in fertile soil, keep pH 6-7, use compost or NPK if needed.

steps.title: Check Your Soil Health
points: pH targets: maize/cereals 5.5–7.0, beans/legumes 6.0–7.5, vegetables 6.0–6.8.
Use a local soil pH test kit or lab for testing.
Too acidic (<5.5): add lime. Too alkaline (>7.5): add sulfur or compost.

steps.title: Fertilizer & Compost
points: Organic: well-decomposed manure, compost, vermicompost (2–5 tons/ha).
DAP 50–100 kg/ha at planting; Urea 50–100 kg/ha top-dress.
NPK 15:15:15 50–100 kg/ha for balanced growth.
Tip: mix chemical fertilizer with compost.

steps.title: Seed Selection & Treatment
points: Choose certified seeds and resistant varieties.
Treat with fungicide/biofungicide (e.g., Apron, Captan).
Optional: hot water soak 50°C for 10–15 minutes.

steps.title: Field Preparation
points: Remove weeds manually or with herbicides.
Plow/till 2–3 times to aerate.
Ensure drainage; form ridges for rows.
Incorporate compost/fertilizer into topsoil.

steps.title: Irrigation Planning
points: Assess water source for season availability.
Furrow irrigation for cereals; drip for vegetables.
Water lightly before planting; follow crop schedules.

steps.title: Planting Time
points: Cereals: plant at rainy season start (Ethiopia maize June–July).
Legumes: plant after soil warms (often July–August).
Vegetables: early rainy season; avoid waterlogging.

steps.title: Planting Depth
points: Small seeds: 2–3 cm; medium: 3–5 cm; large: 4–6 cm.
Deeper in dry soil, shallower in wet soil.

steps.title: Planting Spacing
points: Maize: 75 cm rows, 25–30 cm plants.
Beans: 40–50 cm rows, 10–15 cm plants.
Vegetables: cabbage 50×50 cm, tomato 60×60 cm.

steps.title: Seed Rate
points: Maize 20–25 kg/ha; beans 60–80 kg/ha.
Vegetables: 3–5 g/m² for small seeds.

steps.title: Companion Planting
points: Maize + beans; cabbage + onion.
Helps reduce pests naturally.

steps.title: Row Orientation
points: Align rows north–south for better sunlight.

steps.title: Seed Treatment at Sowing
points: Fungicide coating prevents damping-off.
Biofertilizer for legumes improves N fixation.
Soak seeds in warm water 10–15 min.

steps.title: Irrigation After Sowing
points: Water lightly after sowing; avoid waterlogging.
Continue watering until seedlings are strong.

steps.title: Fertilization Schedule
points: Cereals: DAP 50–100 kg/ha at planting; Urea 50–100 kg/ha at 4–6 leaves.
Legumes: use Rhizobium; avoid high nitrogen.
Vegetables: compost/manure + NPK 50–100 kg/ha; small N doses later.
Tip: mix organic + chemical fertilizers.

steps.title: Irrigation / Watering
points: Water based on soil moisture and growth stage.
Cereals: germination and flowering are critical.
Vegetables: keep moisture during flowering/fruiting.
Avoid overwatering to prevent root rot.

steps.title: Weed Control
points: Remove weeds early (first 3–4 weeks).
Use mulch to suppress weeds and retain moisture.

steps.title: Pest & Disease Management
points: Pests: stem borers, aphids, armyworms, leaf miners.
Diseases: leaf blight, rust, fungal diseases.
Chemical: Dimethoate, Karate, Mancozeb (local guidance).
Organic: neem, soap solution, ash powder.
Monitor weekly and rotate crops.

steps.title: Soil & Nutrient Management
points: Add compost/manure during growth.
Side-dress Urea 3–4 weeks after planting for high-demand crops.
Avoid excess nitrogen.

steps.title: Other Maintenance Tips
points: Prune damaged leaves; stake tall plants.
Keep records of inputs and dates.

steps.title: Signs of Crop Maturity
points: Cereals: leaves dry; kernels hard; ears detach.
Legumes: pods brown; seeds hard.
Vegetables: full size and color.

steps.title: Harvesting Techniques
points: Cereals: cut stalks or hand-pick ears.
Legumes: pick pods by hand.
Vegetables: use knife/scissors; harvest cool hours.

steps.title: Post-Harvest Handling
points: Sun-dry grains 2–3 days; shade vegetables.
Clean and sort; store in airtight bags or ventilated areas.

steps.title: Transport Tips
points: Use clean baskets/sacks.
Avoid piling too high; handle gently.

steps.title: Know Your Market
points: Check prices before harvesting.
Compare local markets; know demand.

steps.title: Crop Preparation for Sale
points: Sort, clean, and package with clean containers.

steps.title: Storage Before Sale
points: Grains in dry airtight bags; vegetables in cool ventilated areas.
Avoid long storage.

steps.title: Pricing & Negotiation
points: Know average price; negotiate politely.
Consider cooperatives/direct buyers.

steps.title: Timing of Sale
points: Sell when demand is high.
Perishables early morning; non-perishables can be stored.

steps.title: Record-Keeping
points: Track quantity, price, and market location.

steps.title: Identify Common Crop Problems
points: Yellow leaves: nitrogen or water stress.
Stunted growth: soil, pests, or low sunlight.
Wilting: root rot or water shortage.
Spots: fungal or bacterial disease.

steps.title: Soil & Nutrient Problems
points: Nitrogen: apply Urea/manure.
Phosphorus: apply DAP.
Potassium: apply potash.

steps.title: Pest Control
points: Use recommended pesticides or organic options.
Remove affected leaves/plants early.

steps.title: Disease Control
points: Fungicides for fungal diseases.
Remove infected plants; avoid wetting leaves.
Rotate crops.

steps.title: Water & Irrigation Troubleshooting
points: Overwatering: reduce irrigation.
Underwatering: increase frequency.
Check soil moisture 5–10 cm deep.

steps.title: Practical Tips
points: Inspect weekly and keep a notebook.
Ask experts or use AI guidance.

steps.title: Selecting Healthy Animals
points: Choose strong, disease-free cattle suited to region.
Avoid visible defects or unusual behavior.

steps.title: Feeding & Nutrition
points: Daily feed: grass, hay, residues, or silage.
Mineral blocks/salt licks; clean water twice daily.

steps.title: Breeding Practices
points: Natural mating: 1 bull per 20–30 cows.
AI for better genetics; record breeding dates.

steps.title: Vaccination & Health Care
points: Vaccinate for Anthrax, Blackleg, Pasteurellosis.
Deworm every 6 months; isolate sick animals.

steps.title: Housing & Safety
points: Safe pens, dry bedding, good ventilation.
Avoid cold drafts in highland areas.

steps.title: Record-Keeping
points: Track birth dates, breeding, vaccinations, weights.
Use records to plan feeding and market timing.

steps.title: Planting Trees on Your Farm
points: Plant along boundaries or terraces.
Benefits: reduce erosion, add shade, improve fertility.
Trees: Sesbania, Grevillea, Moringa, Acacia.

steps.title: Preventing Soil Erosion
points: Contour farming and terracing.
Cover crops to hold soil.

steps.title: Adding Organic Matter
points: Use compost, manure, or crop residues regularly.
Improves structure and water holding.

steps.title: Sustainable Land Use
points: Rotate crops and allow fallow if needed.
Combine trees, crops, and animals.

steps.title: Water Sources
points: Identify rivers, ponds, wells, or rainwater.
Check quantity and quality before planting.

steps.title: Efficient Irrigation Methods
points: Furrow for cereals; drip for vegetables.
Sprinklers for large areas; manual watering for small plots.

steps.title: Timing of Irrigation
points: Water early morning or late evening.
Keep soil moist, not waterlogged.

steps.title: Drought Management
points: Mulch; plant drought-tolerant crops.
Harvest rainwater in ponds or tanks.

steps.title: Water Conservation Tips
points: Repair leaks and schedule irrigation.
Check moisture 5–10 cm below surface.

steps.title: Monitor Weather and Seasons
points: Observe rainfall patterns.
Use local forecasts or radio.

steps.title: Crop Selection for the Season
points: Choose short-season or drought-tolerant crops if needed.
Avoid sensitive crops during heavy rain/cold.

steps.title: Protect Crops from Extreme Weather
points: Raised beds for heavy rain.
Windbreak trees and shade nets.

steps.title: Record Keeping
points: Track planting dates, rainfall, and performance.

steps.title: Climate-Smart Practices
points: Rotation, intercropping, mulching, composting.

steps.title: Track Expenses
points: Seeds, fertilizers, compost, pesticides, labor, tools.
Use notebook or phone.

steps.title: Track Income
points: Sales from crops, livestock, milk, eggs.
Record quantity, price, buyer.

steps.title: Budgeting for the Season
points: Plan input spending.
Reserve for unexpected problems.

steps.title: Planning for Next Season
points: Review profitable crops and effective treatments.
Decide seed quantities.

steps.title: Accessing Support
points: Keep receipts for subsidies, loans, training, cooperatives.
